skill.name: backlink-guard
skill.description: Guide backlink research, source checks, listing verification, and backlink audits through the backlink-guard CLI. Optional paid APIs add traffic, competitor, and AI citation signals.
skill.summary: Evaluate backlink opportunities and monitor existing links with evidence and user approval.
skill.author: zhuyansen

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts match Markdown formatting, documented optional credentials, ordinary local state, and sample URLs rather than malicious behavior. The setup genuinely installs and executes an external PyPI package, whose implementation is absent from the reviewed file. No evidence found of credential theft, obfuscation, or prompt injection; the instructions require approval for paid runs and submissions.

remediation.issue: Setup executes an external package without including its implementation in the reviewed skill.
remediation.suggestion: Provide release provenance and artifact hashes for review. Require installation consent and run the pinned package in an isolated environment with minimal credentials.

content.user_title: Evaluate Backlinks and Track Listing Quality
content.value_statement: Poor backlink sources can waste outreach time and create link-spam risks. This skill guides evidence-based research, source vetting, and ongoing verification through the backlink-guard CLI.
actual_capabilities: Guide CLI discovery of ranking directories, lists, articles, and other relevant backlink opportunities.
Interpret source-vetting grades, policy flags, audience estimates, and missing checks.
Compare competitor referring domains and early launch channels with the user site.
Guide AI Overview and assistant citation research using optional paid providers.
Verify link attributes and placement, maintain submission logs, and recheck recorded sources.
Summarize backlink audit flags, dead linked pages, and suggested redirect targets without changing redirects.
limitations: Requires an external Python CLI package; its implementation was not included in this review.
Advanced metrics and AI research require optional API keys and paid provider access.
Cannot prove private link sales, Google penalties, ranking credit, or future traffic; some search signals cover only US English.
Static verification misses script-inserted links; cached or blocked checks can limit freshness, and spending caps cover estimates only.

use_cases.title: Choose relevant launch directories
use_cases.description: Review candidate directories for audience, topic fit, and link-spam signals before approving individual submissions.

use_cases.title: Review existing backlink quality
use_cases.description: Summarize anchor patterns, unusual growth, shared-owner networks, and dead linked pages with evidence and limited next steps.

use_cases.title: Research AI citation gaps
use_cases.description: Compare cited sources and assistant search visibility for selected buyer questions after approving provider costs.

prompt_templates.prompt: Check [directory domain] for [my domain] using available free signals. Report missing checks and evidence. Do not submit anything.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Verify a live listing
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify [listing URL] links to [my domain]. Report link attributes, placement, and unreadable content. Ask before changing the submission log.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare competitor opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [my domain] with [competitor domains]. Quote estimated costs and wait for approval. Prioritize shared sources and report budget omissions.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Investigate AI visibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare buyer questions for [product]. Let me select them, then quote paid costs and wait. Compare citations, mentions, and search ranks after approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Studying assistant citation and search gaps

best_practices: Review and isolate the pinned external package before running it with minimal credentials.
Approve estimated costs before paid runs and approve each submission with its exact destination and text.
Keep submission logs current and distinguish observed evidence, missing checks, and estimates.
anti_patterns: Treating a favorable source grade as permission to send submissions or purchase followed links.
Creating links in bulk or ignoring a destination list's contribution rules.
Treating traffic estimates, citation samples, or spam flags as proof of penalties or guaranteed ranking gains.

faq.question: Does this skill submit my project automatically?
faq.answer: The CLI does not submit projects. Any assistant-led submission requires your approval of its exact text and destination.

faq.question: Can I use it without API keys?
faq.answer: Yes. Page checks, verification, and logs work without paid keys, but many metrics and AI research features remain unavailable.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: The instructions require Python 3.10 or newer and backlink-guard 0.11.2, preferably through uvx. The external package was not reviewed here.

faq.question: Can a spending cap guarantee the final bill?
faq.answer: No. The cap checks estimated call prices, and actual provider charges can exceed those estimates. Paid runs require approval.

faq.question: Does a clean result prove Google approves a source?
faq.answer: No. Results are evidence-based signals, not Google's verdict. Private sales, blocked pages, and missing metrics can limit the assessment.

faq.question: Where are logs and cached answers stored?
faq.answer: The instructions specify ~/.backlink-guard for logs, paid answers, and observed networks. BACKLINK_GUARD_STATE changes the location; paid answers are cached for seven days.
